newsitem.title: TUNISIA: Algeria wants to close joint ventures in Tunisia.
newsitem.headline: Algeria wants to close joint ventures in Tunisia.

text.p: Algerian Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia said on Sunday he wants to close Tunisia-based firms jointly owned by the two countries that have been running losses.
Tunisians said before his visit the losses were the result of Algeria refusing to buy from the firms, established near the Algerian border in the 1970s to encourage cooperation between the countries.
"We prefer to close a firm to ease problems (between the countries)," Ouyahia told a press conference at the end of a three-day visit when questionned about the trade row.
He did not name the firms he wanted closed or give a target date.

One joint venture, SACMO, which makes diesel engines, was working at 20 percent capacity and showed a 42 million dinar ($42 million) loss and a 72 million dinars ($72 million) debt to Tunisian banks, the sources said.
Before the visit, Tunisian businessmen had accused Algeria of limiting imports of Tunisian products such as cement in recent months and of refusing to buy from the joint ventures.

Tunisian officials had said exports to Algeria in the first eight months of 1996 fell to 73.9 million dinars ($73.9 million) from 95.8 million dinars in the same period in 1995. Tunisia's imports from Algeria, mainly oil, rose to 100.5 million dinars from 80.6 million dinars.

"We have set up a programme to have the exchanges lead to a complementarity in the consumption and production between Tunisia and Algeria," Ouyahia said, denying there was a crisis in trade relations.
A list of agreements signed on Sunday between the countries at the end of the visit mentioned the education, cultural and social sectors but not economic or trade sectors.

Algeria and Tunisia -- along with Morocco, Mauritania and Libya -- are members of the Arab Maghreb Union, a regional grouping set up in 1989 to establish a common market. So far, no concrete steps have been taken.
